use_cases.UC1: Initial Page State — page loads with file input and upload button in correct default state
use_cases.UC2: File Selection Behavior — selecting files populates input, cancel leaves it empty, re-selection replaces
use_cases.UC3: Successful Upload Flow — uploading a file navigates to success page showing correct file name
use_cases.UC4: No File Selected Validation — submitting without a file triggers server error, no client-side required attribute
use_cases.UC5: Sequential Uploads — uploading multiple files in sequence shows only the current file name each time
use_cases.UC6: File Name Integrity — uploaded file name on success page exactly matches selected name including case and punctuation
use_cases.UC7: Navigation Back from Success Page — browser back returns to upload form, fresh load clears selection
use_cases.UC8: Negative and Boundary Tests — boundary conditions, form attributes, and clean state after navigation

tests.title: Verify upload page loads with file input and upload button
Verify file input is empty on initial page load
Verify upload button is enabled on initial page load
Verify form attributes are configured for file upload
Selecting a valid file populates the file input
Selecting a file with different extension (.json) populates the file input correctly
Selecting a file with .md extension populates the file input correctly
Canceling file chooser leaves file input empty
Selecting a second file replaces the first file in the input
Successfully uploading a .txt file navigates to success page with correct file name
Successfully uploading a .json file shows correct file name on success page
Successfully uploading a .md file shows correct file name on success page
Upload success page displays only the file name, not the full path
Clicking Upload without selecting a file shows server error
File input does not have HTML5 required attribute
Upload button remains enabled when no file is selected
Uploading a second file after a successful upload displays the new file name
Three sequential uploads each display the correct current file name
File name on success page exactly matches selected file name including extension
File name with uppercase letters is preserved on success page
File name with dots and hyphens is preserved on success page
Navigating back from success page returns to upload form
File input retains selected file after navigating back from success page
Fresh page load after navigation back clears file selection
Clicking Upload button multiple times with the same file does not cause errors
File input only accepts single file selection, not multiple
Form submission works even without client-side JavaScript enabled
Navigating away and back to upload page resets to clean state
File input accept attribute is not restrictive (no file type filtering)
Success page does not have a form or upload controls

defects.title: Missing upload-sample.txt test fixture file causes ENOENT failures
steps: Run any test that calls uploadPage.selectFile('upload-sample.txt') or uploadPage.uploadFile('upload-sample.txt').
Playwright attempts to resolve the file path relative to the project root.
defects.expected: The file 'upload-sample.txt' exists in the project root and is successfully attached to the file input via setInputFiles.
defects.actual: ENOENT: no such file or directory, stat '/home/runner/work/OpencartAutomation/OpencartAutomation/upload-sample.txt' — test fails immediately at the selectFile step.
defects.test_ref: TC-UPLOAD-005, TC-UPLOAD-009, TC-UPLOAD-010, TC-UPLOAD-013, TC-UPLOAD-018, TC-UPLOAD-019, TC-UPLOAD-021, TC-UPLOAD-022, TC-UPLOAD-023, TC-UPLOAD-024, TC-UPLOAD-026, TC-UPLOAD-028, TC-UPLOAD-030

defects.title: Intermittent navigation timeouts — page.goto fails with net::ERR_ABORTED or timeout
steps: Playwright calls page.goto(url) in the beforeEach hook.
Navigation either aborts (net::ERR_ABORTED) or exceeds the 45s test timeout.
defects.expected: Page navigates to the upload URL and loads within the configured timeout.
defects.actual: page.goto fails with 'net::ERR_ABORTED; maybe frame was detached?' or 'Test timeout of 45000ms exceeded' — the target application is intermittently unresponsive during the test run.
